designDecisions.decision: The two-runtimes executions seam (createAnalysisAwareExecutions): ordinary sandbox tasks keep the substrate's inline drive (PPR-008's pinned behavior, unchanged); codebase-analysis tasks are created WITHOUT the inline drive because their runtime is the analysis route's own lifecycle composition (create -> authorize -> plan -> queue -> start -> the deterministic analysis -> verify -> pass) over the SAME real single write path.
designDecisions.theCollision: Discovered on the materialized plane during this order's route probing: the substrate's universal inline drive and the analysis route's own drive would BOTH compose the SAME execution — the route's create would return the substrate's terminal receipt before the analysis lifecycle ever ran (a fabricated COMPLETED execution with no analysis, or a double-drive collision on the single write path).
designDecisions.theDispatch: The seam dispatches on the FROZEN route's own pinned vocabulary: src/api/routes/codebase-analysis.ts creates every analysis execution with task.kind 'codebase-analysis' — the only composition-visible signal of 'the analysis route composes THIS execution's runtime'. Every other method delegates to the substrate-wrapped service, which itself delegates unchanged to the REAL service — the single write path (state machine, idempotency arbitration, append-only ledger) is shared by both runtimes and bypassed by NEITHER.
designDecisions.honestConsequence: A codebase-analysis task posted DIRECTLY to POST /executions (not through the analysis route) is created WITHOUT the substrate's drive and stays CREATED — the substrate never masquerades as an analysis runtime it did not run, and no other runtime exists for it on this plane. Never a fabricated terminal receipt. Pinned by the unit test's materialized-shape route-table pin + the honest labels.
designDecisions.alternativesRejected: Wrapping the analysis route's drive INTO the substrate (a second analysis runtime inside the substrate module — duplicates the route's own lifecycle and couples the substrate to the learning module); dispatching inside the substrate on task kind (the substrate is PPR-008's pinned surface — this order does not own it).

designDecisions.decision: The economics chain's governing execution is composed through the executions AUTHORITY (createExecution), NOT the substrate-driven sandbox route.
designDecisions.theConstraint: The economics service journals every economic-action boundary event onto the execution's canonical ledger FIRST (recordStepEvent), and the ledger accepts no step events on a TERMINAL execution — but the substrate's inline drive is the plane's only runtime for ORDINARY sandbox tasks and drives every POST /executions create to a terminal receipt inline, so a sandbox-route executionId is already COMPLETED by the time the economics create runs (the honest INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION 409 this order's probe recorded before the design settled).
designDecisions.theResolution: The economics route's own frozen docstring already names where bounded authorization flows: 'the economics module's own governed seams (agent runtime / composition wiring), not through this directly-required surface'. The composition-level authority call leaves the execution CREATED — exactly the shape the production agent-runtime composition produces (the economics-world integration reference composes the same way). The integration chain proof creates the governing execution through authorities.executions.createExecution (task kind 'payment-checkout', honestly named).
designDecisions.materialTradeOff: On THIS plane, an execution that carries an economic action has no runtime that will drive it to terminal by itself — the chain's own settle/fail transitions carry the economic lifecycle, and the execution remains the ledger/provenance anchor. The alternative (an economics-aware substrate drive for a task vocabulary) would invent a second runtime this order was not authorized to build.

designDecisions.decision: The capability admission port awaits the REAL registry's async construction (createCapabilityRegistry(...).then(registry => createCapabilityEconomicAdmission(registry))), and the construction is awaited inside the cold-start ready gate too.
designDecisions.why: The registry constructor is ASYNC (its code-resident seed catalog is arbitrated through the identical publish path at construction); every admission call still flows through the REAL adapter unchanged. A rejected seed fact fails the ready gate — fail closed, never a silently empty catalog.

designDecisions.decision: The payment rail is the IN-REPO createSimulatedPaymentRail under the honest rail id preview-simulated-rail, disclosed everywhere the module contract carries provenance.
designDecisions.why: The preview NEVER touches an external payment provider (no payment credentials exist on this plane, and none were requested — zero new environment variables). The settlement observations the rail produces carry evidence.simulated: true by the rail adapter's OWN contract; every rail-transaction reference names it (sim:preview-simulated-rail:<n>); the composition fact string discloses 'simulated payment rail — honestly disclosed, no external payment provider'; the evidence record and PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT's new section disclose it again. The 'money' is seeded credits the plane's economic actions reserve against (the $10 grant recorded above), never real funds.
